title: A .custom object extension that renames only label keeps the base package's translated pluralLabel, so every list title keeps the old name
body:
domain:ui#3 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CbPN5UYMnBaNJPJWfG

Finding from the #30311 card thread (os-dev-report 6654022838, `out_of_scope_findings` item 2), measured on a local showcase boot. ⛔ Not a claim. Triage sets lane and grade.

**What happens.** A `.custom` `object_extension` that sets only `label` on an installed object (no `pluralLabel`) is served with the new `label` but the base package's translated `pluralLabel`. List titles read the plural first, so after #30311 (PR #30388) the sidebar and list title still show the old name in its plural form; Studio shows the same served answer.

**Expected** (for the owner to confirm against the label-order ruling of #30062): an override that renames `label` without a `pluralLabel` does not keep the base's plural for the old name: either the served plural follows the override's label, or the override is refused / warned at author time for leaving the plural stale. The fix is in the served label order (`packages/metadata-protocol` / spec), not in the console.

**Reader.** The `/meta` label order for overridden items (`domain:server`, the #30062 lineage), or `domain:spec` if an author-time rule is chosen.

Links: #30311, PR #30388, #30062.
